text:
Luke Evangelista arrived in New Jersey after one of the quietly best seasons in the league. Evolving-Hockey had him sixth among 401 forwards in wins above replacement in Nashville last season, with 44 assists in 56 points, though it also said his results ran ahead of his chances.

The fit is still coming together. He has eight points in 13 games and has gone pointless in four straight, and Mike Fink of The Hockey News figures Sheldon Keefe wants to get the Hischier line going, especially its wingers. The process says that's coming. At 5v5 the Devils get 62% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on, and his teammates have scored 4.3 fewer goals than those chances deserve. That gap usually closes, and when it does the passer gets paid. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him 89th percentile in primary shot assists last season. The Devils are also reshuffling their power play, with Evangelista among those talking about it in a team video. Our projection has 42 to 65 more points.
headline: Evangelista's points are behind his play
